**Conversation Overview**

The user requested help transforming a detailed technical implementation document into a streamlined client-facing guide for their "done-with-you" business model. They operate Luxora, a service helping medspas implement 90-day transformation programs combining CRM automation, Meta advertising, and strategic business milestones. The user clarified that their model provides frameworks and templates with embedded AI prompts rather than a prompt library, allowing clients to customize materials using ChatGPT or Claude while receiving biweekly 30-minute check-ins for guidance.

Claude initially created an overly detailed document, which the user requested be condensed to 1-2 pages for the introduction while keeping the detailed week-by-week implementation intact. The user also corrected several assumptions about their service delivery model, specifying that they don't build membership portals, don't provide prompt libraries, and that client onboarding data is collected via checklist rather than during Week 1. The kickoff process involves a 60-90 minute call presenting the blueprint and market analysis, scheduling biweekly check-ins, and setting the 90-day celebration event date.

Claude then created a complete system including the main client implementation guide, a comprehensive list of 55 deliverables spanning the 90-day program, and sample templates demonstrating the embedded AI prompt approach. Each template follows a consistent structure with frameworks, customizable AI prompts, examples, and step-by-step instructions. The deliverables cover everything from team kickoff presentations and consultation scripts to package architecture, review generation systems, event planning materials, and post-celebration follow-up sequences. The user's approach focuses on providing strategic guidance and proven frameworks while empowering clients to create customized materials that sound authentic to their practice using AI assistance.

**90-Day Implementation Schedule**

How to Use This Schedule

**Welcome to your personalized 90-day transformation journey!**

This schedule is your master implementation roadmap, integrating every
playbook you\'ve received from The Luxora Collective into one cohesive,
actionable timeline.

What Makes This Different

**This isn\'t just a list of tasks.** It\'s a strategic sequencing
system designed to:

• Build foundational systems first (weeks 1-4)

• Layer in revenue-generating activities progressively (weeks 5-8)

• Create momentum with your team before launch (weeks 9-12)

• Culminate in a spectacular celebration event (day 90)

Your Four Core Pillars

Every week focuses on one of four strategic pillars from
TheLuxoraCollective.co:

  ----------------- -----------------------------------------------------
  **Pillar**        **Focus**

  **Revenue**       Package architecture, memberships, laser ROI, pricing
                    optimization

  **Reputation**    Review systems, social proof, testimonials, online
                    presence

  **Operations**    Team training, systems, efficiency, scheduling
                    optimization

  **Marketing**     Campaigns, partnerships, events, content creation,
                    client acquisition
  ----------------- -----------------------------------------------------

How to Execute Each Week

**Step 1: Monday Morning - Review the Week**

Take 30 minutes with your leadership team to read through the week\'s
focus areas and assign ownership for each task.

**Step 2: Daily Check-Ins**

10-minute team huddle each morning to track progress, remove obstacles,
and maintain momentum.

**Step 3: Friday Review**

15 minutes to celebrate wins, document what worked, and prepare for next
week.

**Step 4: Track Everything**

Use the Weekly Tracking Dashboard at the end of this document to monitor
KPIs and adjust course as needed.

Quick Reference Timeline

**30,000-Foot View: Your 90-Day Journey**

  ----------------- ------------------ --------------------------------------
  **Phase**         **Timeline**       **Key Outcomes**

  **Foundation**    Days 1-30          Audit complete, packages created,

  Optimize**                           utilization improving, reviews

  **Launch &        Days 61-90         Event planning complete, systems
  Celebrate**                          optimized, massive 90-day celebration,
                                       results documented

  **Partnership**   Days 91+           Ongoing support, quarterly reviews,
                                       continuous optimization, sustained
                                       growth
  ----------------- ------------------ --------------------------------------

Days 1-30: Foundation Phase

*Goal: Establish systems, complete audits, and prepare your team*

Week 1 (Days 1-7): Audit & Baseline

**Primary Playbook Focus: Laser ROI Playbook (Section 1)**

Day 1: Laser Equipment Audit

□ Complete Laser Audit & Baseline (Laser ROI Playbook, Section 1.1)

□ Calculate current ROI timeline for each device

□ Complete 2-week utilization tracking form

□ Identify your top 3 revenue-generating laser treatments

□ Set 90-day utilization and revenue goals

Day 2: Reputation Foundation

□ Complete Current Reputation Audit (Reputation Playbook, Section 1.1)

□ Document current Google rating and total reviews

□ Claim all platform listings (Google, Facebook, Yelp, RealSelf)

□ Analyze top 3 competitors\' review counts and ratings

□ Set 90-day review generation goal (minimum 75 new reviews)

Day 3: Package Architecture Planning

□ Review Package Architecture Framework (Package Playbook, Part 1-2)

□ Analyze current service menu and pricing

□ Calculate hard costs for all services

□ Identify underutilized equipment for package bundling

□ List your top 10 most-requested treatments

Day 4: Team Kickoff Meeting

□ Hold 90-minute all-staff meeting

□ Present 90-day vision and goals

□ Introduce Luxora playbooks and systems

□ Assign individual team member goals

□ Launch team incentive program

□ Get team buy-in and answer questions

Day 5: Google Business Profile Optimization

□ Complete Google Business Profile 100% (Reputation Playbook, Section
1.2)

□ Upload 20+ high-quality photos (facility, team, before/afters)

□ Add all services with detailed descriptions

□ Enable messaging and Q&A features

□ Create review landing page with QR code

□ Set up weekly Google post schedule

Days 6-7: Pricing Structure & Initial Training

□ Create three-tier pricing for top 5 laser treatments (Laser ROI,
Pillar #1)

□ Design add-on menus for each treatment

□ Build package offerings with payment plans

□ Begin staff consultation training (Laser ROI, Module 2)

□ Practice role-play scenarios for objection handling

□ Document baseline weekly metrics

Week 1 Success Metrics

✓ Laser ROI audit complete

✓ Reputation baseline documented

✓ Team aligned and excited

✓ Google Business Profile optimized

✓ Pricing restructure in progress

Week 2 (Days 8-14): Systems Setup & Training

**Primary Playbook Focus: Reputation Engine (Sections 2-3) + Laser ROI
Training**

Days 8-9: Review Automation Setup

□ Configure SMS automation in your booking software (Reputation, Tactic
#1)

□ Set up automated email sequences (3-touch sequence)

□ Create review request templates (SMS and email)

□ Design QR codes for in-office review requests

□ Set up tracking spreadsheet for review metrics

□ Test automation with 5 dummy appointments

Days 10-11: Package Creation Sprint

□ Finalize 3 signature laser packages (Foundation, Transformation,
Signature)

□ Create value breakdown worksheets for each package

□ Write compelling package names and descriptions

□ Design package presentation binders (Package Playbook, Part 8)

□ Create point-of-sale signage and menu boards

□ Update website with new package information

Days 12-13: Staff Training Intensive

□ Train all staff on reputation system (Reputation, Section 6)

□ Practice review request scripts via role-play

□ Train on package consultation process (Laser ROI, Module 2)

□ Establish commission structure for package sales

□ Create internal competition/incentive program

□ Have each team member practice the perfect consultation

Day 14: Marketing Materials Creation

□ Design in-office signage (table tents, checkout cards)

□ Print review request materials with QR codes

□ Update all staff email signatures with review link

□ Create social media graphics for upcoming campaigns

□ Begin compiling before/after photo library

□ Complete Week 2 team training certification

Week 2 Success Metrics

✓ Review automation live and tested

✓ 3+ signature packages created

✓ All team members trained on systems

✓ Marketing collateral ready

✓ Staff excited and competent

Week 3 (Days 15-21): Soft Launch & Content Creation

**Primary Playbook Focus: Reputation Tactics + Laser Marketing Engine**

Days 15-17: Soft Launch with Existing Clients

□ Begin review requests with current clients only

□ Test all automation workflows with real clients

□ Respond to ALL reviews within 24 hours

□ Offer 2-3 new packages to VIP clients first

□ Document issues and questions from team

□ Track initial package conversion rates

□ Goal: 5-8 package sales this week

Days 18-19: Before/After Content Machine

□ Implement Social Proof Capture System (Reputation, Tactic #3)

□ Get digital photo/video release forms signed

□ Capture 10+ before/after photo sets

□ Record 3-5 video testimonials

□ Create storage system for organizing content

□ Begin posting to Instagram 2-3x per week

Days 20-21: Utilization Optimization

□ Implement off-peak incentive pricing (Laser ROI, Strategy #1)

□ Fill Monday/Friday gaps with discounted slots

□ Launch back-to-back efficiency protocol

□ Cross-train providers on multiple laser devices

□ Analyze first 2 weeks of utilization data

□ Week 3 review meeting to troubleshoot

Week 3 Success Metrics

✓ 10-15 new Google reviews collected

✓ 5-8 package sales closed

✓ 10+ before/after sets documented

✓ Utilization improving (target: 50%+)

✓ Systems running smoothly

Week 4 (Days 22-30): Full Launch & Membership Planning

**Primary Playbook Focus: Membership Playbook + Full System Activation**

Days 22-24: Membership Architecture Design

□ Review Membership Playbook Sections 1-4

□ Design 3-tier membership structure

□ Calculate pricing using Value Equation Formula

□ Create benefit stacking for each tier

□ Design membership cards and welcome kits

□ Configure membership software/portal

Days 25-27: Full Launch to All Clients

□ Launch review requests to ALL clients

□ Announce monthly review contest

□ Activate staff incentive program tracking

□ Email database about new packages

□ Update website with membership teasers

□ Goal: 6-10 package sales this week

Days 28-30: Month 1 Review & Planning

□ Complete Month 1 Reputation Report

□ Analyze laser utilization improvement

□ Review package conversion rates

□ Team performance review and recognition

□ Set Month 2 goals

□ Celebrate wins with team

□ Begin planning 90-day celebration event

Month 1 Targets (Days 1-30)

  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------

  New Google Reviews                  20+ reviews

  Laser Utilization                   55-60% utilization

  Laser Revenue                       \$25,000-\$35,000

  Team Readiness                      All systems operational

Days 31-60: Build & Optimize Phase

*Goal: Launch memberships, optimize marketing, scale revenue systems*

**Key Focus Areas:**

• Membership pre-launch and founding member campaign (Weeks 5-6)

• Multi-platform reputation expansion (Weeks 5-7)

Days 61-90: Launch & Celebrate Phase

*Goal: Execute celebration event, optimize all systems, document

**Key Focus Areas:**

• 90-Day Celebration Event planning and execution (Weeks 9-12)

• System documentation and SOPs (Week 9)

• Marketing campaign intensification (Week 10)

Week 10 Focus: Event Planning & Execution

**90-Day Celebration Event Playbook Integration**

□ Complete all pre-event marketing (4-week countdown from Event

□ Finalize event format (VIP evening or Saturday open house)

□ Book vendors (catering, decor, photographer)

90-Day Targets (Final)

     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    65	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    66	
    67	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    68	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    69	```
    70	
    71	### Page Size
    72	
    73	```javascript
    74	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    75	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    76	sections: [{
    77	  properties: {
    78	    page: {
    79	      size: {
    80	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    81	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    82	      },
    83	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    84	    }
    85	  },
    86	  children: [/* content */]
    87	}]
    88	```
    89	
    90	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
    91	
    92	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
    93	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
    94	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
    95	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
    96	
    97	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
    98	
    99	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   100	
   101	```javascript
   102	const doc = new Document({
   103	  styles: {
   104	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   105	    paragraphStyles: [
   106	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   107	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   108	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   109	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   110	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   111	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   112	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   113	    ]
   114	  },
   115	  sections: [{
   116	    children: [
   117	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   118	    ]
   119	  }]
   120	});
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   124	
   125	```javascript
   126	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   127	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   128	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   129	
   130	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   131	const doc = new Document({
   132	  numbering: {
   133	    config: [
   134	      { reference: "bullets",
   135	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   136	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   137	      { reference: "numbers",
   138	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   139	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   140	    ]
   141	  },
   142	  sections: [{
   143	    children: [
   144	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   145	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   146	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   147	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   148	    ]
   149	  }]
   150	});
   151	
   152	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   153	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   154	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   155	```
   156	
   157	### Tables
   158	
   159	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.
   160	
   161	```javascript
   162	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   163	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   164	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   165	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   166	
   167	new Table({
   168	  width: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }, // Always set table width
   169	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Set at table level (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   170	  rows: [
   171	    new TableRow({
   172	      children: [
   173	        new TableCell({
   174	          borders,
   175	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   176	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   177	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   178	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   179	        })
   180	      ]
   181	    })
   182	  ]
   183	})
   184	```
   185	
   186	**Table width calculation:**
   187	
   188	Use `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` for simplicity, or `WidthType.DXA` for precise control:
   189	
   190	```javascript
   191	// Option 1: Percentage (recommended - automatically fits content area)
   192	width: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }
   193	
   194	// Option 2: DXA (precise control)
   195	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   196	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   197	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
   198	columnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width
   199	```
   200	
   201	**Width rules:**
   202	- Table width must equal the sum of `columnWidths`
   203	- Cell `width` must match corresponding `columnWidth`
   204	- Cell `margins` are internal padding - they reduce content area, not add to cell width
   205	- For full-width tables: use content width (page width minus left and right margins)
   206	
   207	### Images
   208	
   209	```javascript
   210	// CRITICAL: type parameter is REQUIRED
   211	new Paragraph({
   212	  children: [new ImageRun({
   213	    type: "png", // Required: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, svg
   214	    data: fs.readFileSync("image.png"),
   215	    transformation: { width: 200, height: 150 },
   216	    altText: { title: "Title", description: "Desc", name: "Name" } // All three required
   217	  })]
   218	})
   219	```
   220	
   221	### Page Breaks
   222	
   223	```javascript
   224	// CRITICAL: PageBreak must be inside a Paragraph
   225	new Paragraph({ children: [new PageBreak()] })
   226	
   227	// Or use pageBreakBefore
   228	new Paragraph({ pageBreakBefore: true, children: [new TextRun("New page")] })
   229	```
   230	
   231	### Table of Contents
   232	
   233	```javascript
   234	// CRITICAL: Headings must use HeadingLevel ONLY - no custom styles
   235	new TableOfContents("Table of Contents", { hyperlink: true, headingStyleRange: "1-3" })
   236	```
   237	
   238	### Headers/Footers
   239	
   240	```javascript
   241	sections: [{
   242	  properties: {
   243	    page: { margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } } // 1440 = 1 inch
   244	  },
   245	  headers: {
   246	    default: new Header({ children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Header")] })] })
   247	  },
   248	  footers: {
   249	    default: new Footer({ children: [new Paragraph({
   250	      children: [new TextRun("Page "), new TextRun({ children: [PageNumber.CURRENT] })]
   251	    })] })
   252	  },
   253	  children: [/* content */]
   254	}]
   255	```
   256	
   257	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   258	
   259	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   260	- **Never use `\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements
   261	- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config
   262	- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML
   263	- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc
   264	- **Always set table `width`** - use `{ size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }` for full width
   265	- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match
   266	- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly
   267	- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding
   268	- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading
   269	- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs
   270	- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: "Heading1", "Heading2", etc.
   271	- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)
   272	
   273	---
   274	
   275	## Editing Existing Documents
   276	
   277	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   278	
   279	### Step 1: Unpack
   280	```bash
   281	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   282	```
   283	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   284	
   285	### Step 2: Edit XML
   286	
   287	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   288	
   289	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   290	
   291	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   292	
   293	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   294	```xml
   295	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   296	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   297	```
   298	| Entity | Character |
   299	|--------|-----------|
   300	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   301	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   302	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   303	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   304	
   305	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   306	```bash
   307	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   308	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   309	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   310	```
   311	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   312	
   313	### Step 3: Pack
   314	```bash
   315	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   316	```
   317	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   318	
   319	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   320	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   321	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   322	
   323	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   324	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   325	
   326	### Common Pitfalls
   327	
   328	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   329	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   330	
   331	---
   332	
   333	## XML Reference
   334	
   335	### Schema Compliance
   336	
   337	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   338	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   339	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   340	
   341	### Tracked Changes
   342	
   343	**Insertion:**
   344	```xml
   345	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   346	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   347	</w:ins>
   348	```
   349	
   350	**Deletion:**
   351	```xml
   352	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   353	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   354	</w:del>
   355	```
   356	
   357	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   358	
   359	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   360	```xml
   361	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   362	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   363	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   364	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   365	</w:del>
   366	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   367	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   368	</w:ins>
   369	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   370	```
   371	
   372	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   373	```xml
   374	<w:p>
   375	  <w:pPr>
   376	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   377	    <w:rPr>
   378	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   379	    </w:rPr>
   380	  </w:pPr>
   381	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   382	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   383	  </w:del>
   384	</w:p>

# WEEK 1 DELIVERABLE: Consultation Script Framework

## How to Use This Template

1. Read through the consultation flow framework
2. Use the AI prompts to customize for your specific treatments
3. Train your team using the customized scripts
4. Practice with role-play scenarios (included at bottom)

---

## CONSULTATION FLOW FRAMEWORK

### STEP 1: Opening & Rapport Building (2 minutes)

**Template Script:**
"Hi [Client Name]! I'm [Your Name]. I'm so glad you're here today. Before we dive in, tell me a little bit about what brought you in and what you're hoping to achieve."

**Listen actively, take notes, repeat back what you heard**

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create 3 variations of an opening rapport-building script for laser treatment 
consultations at my medspa. The tone should be: [warm/professional/medical/casual]. 
Our ideal clients are [DEMOGRAPHIC] who typically come in for [MAIN CONCERNS]. 
Make it conversational and welcoming, not salesy.
```

---

### STEP 2: Discovery Questions (5 minutes)

**Template Question Flow:**

1. **The Concern:** "What specific areas are you looking to address?"

2. **Previous Experience:** "Have you tried any treatments for this before? What worked or didn't work?"

3. **Timeline:** "Is there a specific event or timeframe you're working toward?"

4. **Investment Mindset:** "Have you researched treatment options? What's most important to you - results, timeline, or budget?"

5. **Decision Process:** "Are you the only decision-maker, or is someone else involved in this decision?"

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create a discovery question framework for [SPECIFIC TREATMENT like: laser hair removal, 
skin resurfacing, body contouring]. I need 5-7 questions that uncover: the client's 
specific concerns, previous treatments tried, timeline/urgency, budget awareness, and 
decision-making process. Make the questions feel natural, not interrogative.
```

---

### STEP 3: Education & Solution Presentation (10 minutes)

**Template Framework:**

**The Problem (Mirror back their concern):**
"Based on what you've told me, you're dealing with [THEIR CONCERN]. This is really common, and here's why it happens..."

**The Solution (Your treatment):**
"The best solution for what you're describing is [TREATMENT]. Let me show you how it works..."

**The Process (Set expectations):**
"Here's exactly what you can expect: [NUMBER] treatments, spaced [TIMEFRAME] apart. Each session takes [TIME]. You'll start seeing results after [TIMELINE]."

**The Results (Show proof):**
"Let me show you some before/after photos from clients with similar concerns..."

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create an education script for [SPECIFIC TREATMENT]. Include:
- Simple explanation of how the treatment works (no jargon)
- Typical treatment timeline ([X] sessions over [X] weeks)
- When they'll see results
- What they'll experience during treatment
- Realistic before/after expectations

Make it confident but not overpromising. Our ideal client is [DEMOGRAPHIC] 
who values [results/speed/comfort/etc.].
```

---

### STEP 4: Package Presentation (7 minutes)

**Template Framework:**

**The Single Treatment Option (Anchor high):**
"If you were to do this treatment individually, each session is [$X], so for the [NUMBER] treatments you need, that would be [$TOTAL]."

**The Package Option (Show value):**
"Now, what most of our clients do is invest in one of our treatment packages because you save significantly and get better results by committing to the full series upfront."

**Present Your 3 Tiers:**

**FOUNDATION Package** - [$X]
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**TRANSFORMATION Package** - [$X] (MOST POPULAR)
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
- [BENEFIT 3]
- [BONUS]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**SIGNATURE Package** - [$X]
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
- [BENEFIT 3]
- [BONUS 1]
- [BONUS 2]
- [VIP PERK]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**The Close:**
"Based on what you've told me about [THEIR CONCERN] and your goals, I'd recommend the [PACKAGE NAME] because [SPECIFIC REASON]."

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create a 3-tier package presentation script for [TREATMENT TYPE]. 

Current pricing:
- Single treatment: [$X]
- Recommended series: [X] treatments

Create three packages:
1. Foundation (entry level, basic series)
2. Transformation (mid-tier, most popular, best value)
3. Signature (premium, with VIP perks)

Include pricing, what's included, and who each package is best for. Make the 
Transformation package the obvious best value. Include a natural way to recommend 
the right package based on what they told me in discovery.
```

---

### STEP 5: Objection Handling (5 minutes)

**Common Objections & Responses:**

**"I need to think about it."**
Response: "I totally understand - this is an investment. Can I ask what specifically you'd like to think about? Is it the timeline, the investment, or something about the treatment itself?"

[Then address the real concern]

**"That's more than I expected to spend."**
Response: "I appreciate you being upfront about that. Let me ask - when you think about the result you want [THEIR GOAL], what would that be worth to you? Also, we have payment plans as low as [$X/month] that might work better for your budget."

**"I want to shop around and compare."**
Response: "Smart move - you should feel confident in your choice. What other options are you looking at? I'm happy to help you understand the differences so you can make the best decision."

**"I need to talk to my spouse/partner."**
Response: "Of course! Would it help if I put together everything we discussed in writing so you can share it with them? Or would they want to come in for a consultation too? I'm happy to meet with both of you."

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create objection handling scripts for these common responses to [TREATMENT] packages:

1. "I need to think about it"
2. "That's too expensive"
3. "I want to shop around"
4. "I need to talk to [spouse/partner]"
5. "Can I just do one treatment and see?"

For each objection, provide:
- A question to uncover the real concern
- A value-reframe response
- A path forward that keeps the conversation going

Tone should be: consultative, not pushy. Focus on helping them make the 
right decision, not just closing the sale.
```

---

### STEP 6: Closing & Next Steps (3 minutes)

**Template Script:**

**If they're ready to book:**
"Amazing! Let's get you scheduled. Based on what we discussed, we'll want to start with [FIRST TREATMENT] on [DATE], and then space your treatments [TIMEFRAME] apart. Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?"

[Book the series, collect payment/deposit]

**If they're not ready:**
"No pressure at all. Here's what I'll do - I'll send you an email with everything we discussed, the package details, and some before/after photos. Do you mind if I follow up with you in [2-3 days] to answer any questions that come up?"

[Get their email, set follow-up task in CRM]

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create closing scripts for two scenarios:

1. Client is ready to move forward: How do I smoothly transition to booking 
   and payment without being awkward?

2. Client needs time: How do I set up follow-up without being pushy? What 
   should I send them? When should I follow up?

Include specific language for scheduling the treatment series and explaining 
the payment process. Keep it natural and service-oriented.
```

---

## BONUS: ADD-ON PRESENTATION

**When to present add-ons:** After they've committed to a package, before final payment

**Template Script:**
"Perfect! One more thing I want to mention - a lot of our clients who do [MAIN TREATMENT] also add [ADD-ON TREATMENT] because it enhances the results and helps you get there faster. It's only an additional [$X] if you add it today, versus [$Y] if you add it later. Would you like me to include that?"

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create add-on presentation scripts for [MAIN TREATMENT] packages. Our most 
popular add-ons are:
1. [ADD-ON 1] - enhances results by [BENEFIT]
2. [ADD-ON 2] - speeds up results by [BENEFIT]
3. [ADD-ON 3] - maintains results by [BENEFIT]

Create natural language to present these AFTER they've committed to the main 
package. Include pricing incentive for adding now vs later. Make it feel like 
I'm helping them get better results, not upselling.
```

---

## ROLE-PLAY SCENARIOS FOR TEAM TRAINING

### Scenario 1: The Motivated Buyer
**Client Profile:** Excited, ready to invest, just wants to know it works
**Focus:** Confidence, social proof, closing

### Scenario 2: The Price Shopper
**Client Profile:** Asking about discounts, comparing to competitors, budget-conscious
**Focus:** Value demonstration, payment plans, ROI

### Scenario 3: The Skeptic
**Client Profile:** Tried other treatments, didn't work, worried about results
**Focus:** Education, managing expectations, risk reversal

### Scenario 4: The Indecisive
**Client Profile:** Interested but can't commit, needs to "think about it"
**Focus:** Uncovering real objection, creating urgency, follow-up

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE CUSTOM ROLE-PLAYS:**
```
Create 4 detailed role-play scenarios for training my team on [TREATMENT] 
consultations. For each scenario include:

1. Client persona (background, concerns, personality type, objections)
2. What the team member should focus on
3. Key phrases to practice
4. How to successfully close or advance the conversation

Make them realistic based on the actual clients we see. Our typical clients 
are [DEMOGRAPHIC] with [COMMON CONCERNS].
```

---

## CONSULTATION TIMING GUIDE

**Total Time: 30 minutes**
- Opening & Rapport: 2 min
- Discovery: 5 min
- Education: 10 min
- Package Presentation: 7 min
- Objection Handling: 5 min
- Closing: 3 min
- Buffer: 3 min

**Pro Tip:** Set a 30-minute timer and practice hitting each section on time. 
Efficient consultations convert better than long, rambling ones.

---

## MASTER AI PROMPT - Generate Complete Consultation Script

```
Create a complete consultation script for [SPECIFIC TREATMENT] at my medspa.

Practice details:
- Treatment: [TREATMENT NAME]
- Target client: [DEMOGRAPHIC, AGE RANGE, CONCERNS]
- Typical series: [X] treatments over [X] weeks
- Single treatment price: [$X]
- Package prices: Foundation [$X], Transformation [$X], Signature [$X]

Include:
1. Opening rapport builder
2. 5-7 discovery questions
3. Treatment education (benefits, process, timeline, results)
4. 3-tier package presentation with value stack
5. Responses to 5 common objections
6. Closing language for "yes" and "not yet" scenarios
7. Add-on presentation for [ADD-ON TREATMENTS]

Tone: [Professional/warm/medical/conversational]
Goal: Convert at least 60% of qualified consultations
```

---

**VIDEO TUTORIAL:** [Link to video showing consultation flow and script usage]

**EXAMPLE:** [Link to recorded example consultation using this script]

**PRACTICE TOOL:** [Link to interactive role-play scenarios]

**FOUNDATION Package** - [$X]
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**TRANSFORMATION Package** - [$X] (MOST POPULAR)
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
- [BENEFIT 3]
- [BONUS]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**SIGNATURE Package** - [$X]
- [NUMBER] treatments
- [BENEFIT 1]
- [BENEFIT 2]
- [BENEFIT 3]
- [BONUS 1]
- [BONUS 2]
- [VIP PERK]
Best for: [WHO IT'S FOR]

**The Close:**
"Based on what you've told me about [THEIR CONCERN] and your goals, I'd recommend the [PACKAGE NAME] because [SPECIFIC REASON]."

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create a 3-tier package presentation script for [TREATMENT TYPE]. 

Current pricing:
- Single treatment: [$X]
- Recommended series: [X] treatments

Create three packages:
1. Foundation (entry level, basic series)
2. Transformation (mid-tier, most popular, best value)
3. Signature (premium, with VIP perks)

Include pricing, what's included, and who each package is best for. Make the 
Transformation package the obvious best value. Include a natural way to recommend 
the right package based on what they told me in discovery.
```

---

### STEP 5: Objection Handling (5 minutes)

**Common Objections & Responses:**

**"I need to think about it."**
Response: "I totally understand - this is an investment. Can I ask what specifically you'd like to think about? Is it the timeline, the investment, or something about the treatment itself?"

[Then address the real concern]

**"That's more than I expected to spend."**
Response: "I appreciate you being upfront about that. Let me ask - when you think about the result you want [THEIR GOAL], what would that be worth to you? Also, we have payment plans as low as [$X/month] that might work better for your budget."

**"I want to shop around and compare."**
Response: "Smart move - you should feel confident in your choice. What other options are you looking at? I'm happy to help you understand the differences so you can make the best decision."

**"I need to talk to my spouse/partner."**
Response: "Of course! Would it help if I put together everything we discussed in writing so you can share it with them? Or would they want to come in for a consultation too? I'm happy to meet with both of you."

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create objection handling scripts for these common responses to [TREATMENT] packages:

1. "I need to think about it"
2. "That's too expensive"
3. "I want to shop around"
4. "I need to talk to [spouse/partner]"
5. "Can I just do one treatment and see?"

For each objection, provide:
- A question to uncover the real concern
- A value-reframe response
- A path forward that keeps the conversation going

Tone should be: consultative, not pushy. Focus on helping them make the 
right decision, not just closing the sale.
```

---

### STEP 6: Closing & Next Steps (3 minutes)

**Template Script:**

**If they're ready to book:**
"Amazing! Let's get you scheduled. Based on what we discussed, we'll want to start with [FIRST TREATMENT] on [DATE], and then space your treatments [TIMEFRAME] apart. Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?"

[Book the series, collect payment/deposit]

**If they're not ready:**
"No pressure at all. Here's what I'll do - I'll send you an email with everything we discussed, the package details, and some before/after photos. Do you mind if I follow up with you in [2-3 days] to answer any questions that come up?"

[Get their email, set follow-up task in CRM]

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create closing scripts for two scenarios:

1. Client is ready to move forward: How do I smoothly transition to booking 
   and payment without being awkward?

2. Client needs time: How do I set up follow-up without being pushy? What 
   should I send them? When should I follow up?

Include specific language for scheduling the treatment series and explaining 
the payment process. Keep it natural and service-oriented.
```

---

## BONUS: ADD-ON PRESENTATION

**When to present add-ons:** After they've committed to a package, before final payment

**Template Script:**
"Perfect! One more thing I want to mention - a lot of our clients who do [MAIN TREATMENT] also add [ADD-ON TREATMENT] because it enhances the results and helps you get there faster. It's only an additional [$X] if you add it today, versus [$Y] if you add it later. Would you like me to include that?"

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create add-on presentation scripts for [MAIN TREATMENT] packages. Our most 
popular add-ons are:
1. [ADD-ON 1] - enhances results by [BENEFIT]
2. [ADD-ON 2] - speeds up results by [BENEFIT]
3. [ADD-ON 3] - maintains results by [BENEFIT]

Create natural language to present these AFTER they've committed to the main 
package. Include pricing incentive for adding now vs later. Make it feel like 
I'm helping them get better results, not upselling.
```

---

## ROLE-PLAY SCENARIOS FOR TEAM TRAINING

### Scenario 1: The Motivated Buyer
**Client Profile:** Excited, ready to invest, just wants to know it works
**Focus:** Confidence, social proof, closing

### Scenario 2: The Price Shopper
**Client Profile:** Asking about discounts, comparing to competitors, budget-conscious
**Focus:** Value demonstration, payment plans, ROI

### Scenario 3: The Skeptic
**Client Profile:** Tried other treatments, didn't work, worried about results
**Focus:** Education, managing expectations, risk reversal

### Scenario 4: The Indecisive
**Client Profile:** Interested but can't commit, needs to "think about it"
**Focus:** Uncovering real objection, creating urgency, follow-up

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE CUSTOM ROLE-PLAYS:**
```

1. Client persona (background, concerns, personality type, objections)
2. What the team member should focus on
3. Key phrases to practice
4. How to successfully close or advance the conversation

Make them realistic based on the actual clients we see. Our typical clients 
are [DEMOGRAPHIC] with [COMMON CONCERNS].
```

---

**Total Time: 30 minutes**
- Opening & Rapport: 2 min
- Discovery: 5 min
- Education: 10 min
- Package Presentation: 7 min
- Objection Handling: 5 min
- Closing: 3 min
- Buffer: 3 min

**Pro Tip:** Set a 30-minute timer and practice hitting each section on time. 
Efficient consultations convert better than long, rambling ones.

---

- Typical series: [X] treatments over [X] weeks
- Single treatment price: [$X]
- Package prices: Foundation [$X], Transformation [$X], Signature [$X]

Include:
1. Opening rapport builder
2. 5-7 discovery questions
3. Treatment education (benefits, process, timeline, results)
4. 3-tier package presentation with value stack
5. Responses to 5 common objections
6. Closing language for "yes" and "not yet" scenarios
7. Add-on presentation for [ADD-ON TREATMENTS]

Tone: [Professional/warm/medical/conversational]
Goal: Convert at least 60% of qualified consultations
```

---

**EXAMPLE:** [Link to recorded example consultation using this script]

# WEEK 2 DELIVERABLE: Package Architecture Framework

## How to Use This Template

1. Complete the pricing calculator section first
2. Use AI prompts to create your 3 signature packages
3. Build value breakdown worksheets
4. Create presentation materials

---

## PART 1: PRICING CALCULATOR

### Step 1: Calculate Your Hard Costs

**For Each Treatment Type, Document:**

| Item | Cost |
|------|------|
| Equipment cost per session (depreciation) | $____ |
| Consumables (tips, gel, etc.) | $____ |
| Provider time (hourly rate ÷ treatments per hour) | $____ |
| Overhead allocation | $____ |
| **TOTAL HARD COST PER TREATMENT** | **$____** |

**AI PROMPT TO CALCULATE:**
```
Help me calculate the true cost per treatment for [TREATMENT TYPE].

Equipment details:
- Equipment cost: [$X]
- Expected lifespan: [X] treatments OR [X] years
- Treatments per hour: [X]

Consumables per treatment:
- [ITEM 1]: [$X]
- [ITEM 2]: [$X]
- [ITEM 3]: [$X]

Labor:
- Provider hourly rate: [$X]
- Treatment duration: [X] minutes

Overhead:
- Monthly overhead: [$X]
- Monthly treatments: [X]

Calculate my cost per treatment and recommended pricing to hit [X]% profit margin.
```

---

### Step 2: Determine Your Single Treatment Price

**Formula:** Hard Cost × 3-5 = Single Treatment Price

**Example:**
- Hard Cost: $50
- Single Treatment Price: $150-250
- Your Choice: $___

**AI PROMPT TO DETERMINE PRICING:**
```
I need to price [TREATMENT TYPE] in [YOUR CITY/MARKET]. 

My costs:
- Hard cost per treatment: [$X]
- Recommended treatments in series: [X]

Competitive landscape:
- Competitor 1 charges: [$X]
- Competitor 2 charges: [$X]
- Competitor 3 charges: [$X]

My positioning: [Luxury/mid-market/value]
My ideal client: [DEMOGRAPHIC]

What should I charge for:
1. Single treatment
2. Series of [X] (should show savings but maintain margin)

Explain your reasoning based on market positioning and profitability.
```

---

### Step 3: Create Your Package Tiers

**The Formula:**

**FOUNDATION (Entry Level)**
- Core treatments only
- Minimal extras
- Price: 15-20% savings vs à la carte

**TRANSFORMATION (Most Popular - Your Profit Center)**
- Core treatments
- Strategic add-ons
- Valuable bonuses
- Price: 25-30% savings vs à la carte
- **Goal: 60-70% of clients choose this**

**SIGNATURE (Premium/VIP)**
- Core treatments
- Multiple add-ons
- Exclusive perks
- VIP experience
- Price: 30-40% savings vs à la carte

---

## PART 2: BUILD YOUR PACKAGES

### Package Template Structure

For each treatment type, create 3 packages using this framework:

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE PACKAGES:**
```
Create 3 treatment packages for [SPECIFIC TREATMENT like: Laser Hair Removal, 
RF Microneedling, Body Contouring].

Treatment details:
- Single treatment price: [$X]
- Recommended series: [X] treatments
- Session duration: [X] minutes
- Results timeline: [WHEN THEY SEE RESULTS]

Available add-ons that enhance results:
- [ADD-ON 1]: [$X value]
- [ADD-ON 2]: [$X value]
- [ADD-ON 3]: [$X value]

Available bonuses I can include:
- [BONUS 1]: [$X value]
- [BONUS 2]: [$X value]

Create three packages:

1. FOUNDATION Package
   - Include: core treatments only
   - Price: [Show 15-20% savings]
   - Best for: [Type of client]

2. TRANSFORMATION Package (MOST POPULAR)
   - Include: core treatments + [1-2 add-ons] + [1 bonus]
   - Price: [Show 25-30% savings]
   - Best for: [Type of client]
   - Why this is best value: [Explain]

3. SIGNATURE Package
   - Include: core treatments + [2-3 add-ons] + [2+ bonuses] + [VIP perk]
   - Price: [Show 30-40% savings]
   - Best for: [Type of client]

For each package provide:
- Compelling package name (not just "Bronze/Silver/Gold")
- Complete inclusions list
- Total value breakdown
- Actual package price
- Savings amount
- "Best for" client description
```

---

## PART 3: PACKAGE NAMING

**Bad Package Names:** (Don't use these)
- Bronze/Silver/Gold
- Basic/Standard/Premium
- Package A/B/C
- Small/Medium/Large

**Good Package Names:** (Use these principles)
- Outcome-focused
- Emotionally resonant
- Treatment-specific
- Aspirational

**AI PROMPT FOR NAMING:**
```
Create compelling names for 3 treatment packages for [SPECIFIC TREATMENT].

The packages are:
1. Entry level: [X] treatments, focused on [OUTCOME]
2. Mid-tier (most popular): [X] treatments + [ADD-ONS], focused on [BETTER OUTCOME]
3. Premium: [X] treatments + [PREMIUM ADD-ONS], focused on [BEST OUTCOME]

Our ideal client is: [DEMOGRAPHIC]
The main benefit they want: [DESIRED OUTCOME]
Our brand voice is: [Luxury/clinical/approachable/modern]

Generate 3-5 name options for each tier. Names should be:
- 1-3 words maximum
- Outcome or benefit focused
- Memorable and distinct
- Aligned with our brand

Example good names: "Smooth & Confident", "Complete Transformation", 
"Ultimate Radiance", "Express Glow", "Total Renewal"
```

---

## PART 4: VALUE BREAKDOWN WORKSHEET

Create this one-page document for each package to use during consultations.

**Template Structure:**

---
**[PACKAGE NAME] PACKAGE**

**What's Included:**
□ [X] [Treatment Name] sessions ([$X] value each) = [$X]
□ [Add-on 1] ([$X] value) = [$X]
□ [Add-on 2] ([$X] value) = [$X]
□ [Bonus 1] ([$X] value) = [$X]
□ [Bonus 2] ([$X] value) = [$X]

**Total À La Carte Value: $____**
**Your Package Price: $____**
**YOU SAVE: $____ ([X]% savings)**

**Payment Options:**
- Pay in full: $____ (save additional [$X])
- Payment plan: $____/month for [X] months

**Treatment Timeline:**
- Session 1: [WEEK]
- Session 2: [WEEK]
- Session 3: [WEEK]
- Results visible: [TIMELINE]
- Final results: [TIMELINE]

**Best For:**
[Description of ideal client for this package]

**Why Clients Choose This:**
"[Testimonial or key benefit statement]"
---

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE VALUE BREAKDOWN:**
```
Create a value breakdown worksheet for my [PACKAGE NAME] package.

Package includes:
- [X] [Treatment type] sessions at [$X] each
- [Add-on 1] worth [$X]
- [Add-on 2] worth [$X]
- [Bonus 1] worth [$X]
- [Bonus 2] worth [$X]

Package price: [$X]
Payment plan option: [$X]/month for [X] months

Treatment schedule: [X] sessions spaced [TIMEFRAME] apart
Results timeline: [WHEN THEY SEE RESULTS]

Create a visual one-page breakdown that clearly shows:
1. Everything included with values
2. Total à la carte value
3. Package price
4. Savings amount and percentage
5. Payment options
6. Treatment timeline
7. Who this package is best for
8. A compelling reason why clients choose it

Format it so a front desk person can easily present it and the value is 
immediately obvious.
```

---

## PART 5: PACKAGE PRESENTATION BINDER

Create a physical binder or digital presentation with:

**Page 1: Cover**
- "[Treatment Type] Packages"
- Your logo
- Beautiful imagery

**Page 2-3: The Problem & Solution**
- What [concern] is and why it happens
- How [treatment] solves it
- Before/after examples

**Page 4: Treatment Series Recommendation**
- Why multiple treatments are needed
- Expected results timeline
- What to expect during treatments

**Pages 5-7: Your Three Packages**
- One full page per package
- Package name prominently displayed
- Visual value breakdown
- Compelling imagery
- "Most Popular" badge on Transformation

**Page 8: Before/After Gallery**
- 6-12 powerful before/after images
- Real clients (with permission)
- Similar concerns to prospects

**Page 9: Payment Options**
- Pay in full discount
- Monthly payment plans
- Accepted payment methods
- Financing options (if available)

**Page 10: What Happens Next**
- Booking process
- Pre-treatment instructions
- What to expect at first appointment

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE BINDER CONTENT:**
```
Create content for a package presentation binder for [TREATMENT TYPE] packages.

I need compelling copy for:

1. Opening section - The Problem
   - Describe [CONCERN/CONDITION] in empathetic terms
   - Why it happens
   - How common it is

2. The Solution section
   - How [TREATMENT] works (in simple terms)
   - Why [X] treatments are needed
   - Timeline for results
   - Safety and comfort information

3. Three package pages (one per package):
   Package 1: [NAME] - [$PRICE]
   [INCLUSIONS]
   
   Package 2: [NAME] - [$PRICE] (MOST POPULAR)
   [INCLUSIONS]
   
   Package 3: [NAME] - [$PRICE]
   [INCLUSIONS]

For each package page, write:
- Headline that sells the outcome
- 2-3 sentences on who it's perfect for
- Bullet points of what's included
- A compelling "imagine this" statement about the results

4. Closing section
   - How to get started
   - Payment options
   - What happens next

Tone: [Professional/warm/medical/luxury]
Keep it client-focused, benefit-driven, and easy to scan.
```

---

## PART 6: SIGNAGE & MARKETING COLLATERAL

### Table Tent Copy

**Template:**
---
**[PACKAGE NAME]**

Get [DESIRED OUTCOME] with our [TREATMENT] package

✓ [BENEFIT 1]
✓ [BENEFIT 2]
✓ [BENEFIT 3]

Starting at $____/month

Ask us about our packages today!
---

**AI PROMPT FOR TABLE TENTS:**
```
Create copy for 3 table tent cards (4"x6") promoting our [TREATMENT] packages.

Each should highlight:
- Package name
- Main outcome/benefit
- 3 key features or benefits (checkmarks)
- Starting payment option
- Clear call to action

Keep each to under 30 words total. Make them scannable and compelling.

Our packages:
1. [PACKAGE 1 NAME] - [MAIN BENEFIT]
2. [PACKAGE 2 NAME] - [MAIN BENEFIT]
3. [PACKAGE 3 NAME] - [MAIN BENEFIT]

Tone: [YOUR BRAND VOICE]
```

### Checkout Card Copy

**Template:**
---
**Before You Go...**

Did you know you can save up to [X]% with our [Treatment] packages?

Most clients see better results and spend less by committing to a complete series.

**Ask us about:**
→ [Package 1 Name] - [One-line benefit]
→ [Package 2 Name] - [One-line benefit]
→ [Package 3 Name] - [One-line benefit]

**Ready to upgrade?** We can switch you today!
---

**AI PROMPT FOR CHECKOUT CARDS:**
```
Write copy for a checkout counter card promoting our [TREATMENT] packages 
to existing single-treatment clients.

Goal: Encourage them to upgrade to a package before they leave

Include:
- Attention-grabbing headline
- Brief value proposition (why packages are better)
- Quick overview of 3 packages
- Easy next step

Keep it under 50 words. Make the decision easy and immediate.
```

### Menu Board Copy

**AI PROMPT FOR MENU BOARD:**
```
Create a service menu board layout for [TREATMENT TYPE] with our 3 packages.

For each package display:
- Package name
- One-line description
- Price (or starting at $X/mo)
- "Most Popular" badge for mid-tier

Also include:
- Single treatment option (priced higher to anchor)
- "Ask us which package is right for you" footer

Format should be easy to read from 6-8 feet away. Use hierarchy and white 
space effectively.
```

---

## PART 7: SAMPLE PACKAGES BY TREATMENT TYPE

### Example: Laser Hair Removal Packages

**SMOOTH & CONFIDENT Package** - $1,499
- 6 laser hair removal treatments
- Small area (underarms OR bikini line)
- Best for: First-time clients

**TOTAL TRANSFORMATION Package** - $2,999 ⭐ MOST POPULAR
- 8 laser hair removal treatments
- Large area (full legs OR Brazilian + underarms)
- Free numbing cream ($50 value)
- Best for: Complete coverage

**ULTIMATE FREEDOM Package** - $4,999
- 10 laser hair removal treatments
- Multiple large areas (full legs + Brazilian + underarms)
- Free numbing cream ($50 value)
- Free touch-up session (6 months post-treatment)
- VIP scheduling priority
- Best for: Total body smoothness

**AI PROMPT TO CREATE TREATMENT-SPECIFIC PACKAGES:**
```
Using the package framework, create 3 packages for [YOUR SPECIFIC TREATMENT].

Treatment details:
- Treatment type: [NAME]
- Typical series length: [X] treatments
- Single treatment price: [$X]
- Treatment areas: [LIST OPTIONS]
- Available add-ons: [LIST]
- Typical client goals: [GOALS]

Create three compelling packages with names, pricing, inclusions, and 
"best for" descriptions that would appeal to [YOUR IDEAL CLIENT].
```

---

## MASTER AI PROMPT - Complete Package Creation

```
I need to create a complete 3-tier package system for [TREATMENT TYPE] at my medspa.

Current situation:
- Treatment type: [NAME]
- Single treatment price: [$X]
- My hard cost per treatment: [$X]
- Recommended treatment series: [X] treatments
- Treatment duration: [X] minutes

Available add-ons that enhance results:
- [ADD-ON 1]: [$X value, benefit]
- [ADD-ON 2]: [$X value, benefit]
- [ADD-ON 3]: [$X value, benefit]

Bonuses I can include:
- [BONUS 1]: [$X value]
- [BONUS 2]: [$X value]

Target market: [DEMOGRAPHIC, BUDGET, GOALS]
Brand positioning: [Luxury/medical/approachable]

Create:
1. Three package names (outcome-focused, not Bronze/Silver/Gold)
2. Complete package structures (what's included in each)
3. Pricing strategy (show savings, maintain margin)
4. Value breakdown for each package
5. "Best for" descriptions for each tier
6. Key selling points that differentiate each package
7. Payment plan options
8. Presentation copy I can use in consultations

Goal: 60% of clients should choose the middle tier. Make that the obvious 
best value while still making the premium tier tempting for those who want 
the absolute best.
```

---

**VIDEO TUTORIAL:** [Link to video walkthrough of package creation process]

**CALCULATOR TOOL:** [Link to pricing calculator spreadsheet]

**EXAMPLES:** [Link to 10+ example package structures from other practices]

2. Customize the message templates with AI prompts

### The 3-Touch Sequence

**Touch 1: Immediately After Appointment (Within 1 hour)**
- Method: Automated SMS
- Purpose: Capture enthusiasm while experience is fresh
- Conversion Rate: Highest (60-70%)

**Touch 2: 24 Hours Later (If no review yet)**
- Method: Automated Email
- Purpose: Gentle reminder with different angle
- Conversion Rate: Medium (20-30%)

**Touch 3: 3 Days Later (If still no review)**
- Method: Personal text from provider
- Purpose: One final personal request
- Conversion Rate: Lower (10-15%)

**Stop after Touch 3** - Don't become annoying

---

## PART 2: SMS TEMPLATES (Touch 1 - Automated)

### Template A: Simple & Direct

**Template:**
```
Hi [First Name]! Thanks for visiting us today. We'd love to hear about your 
experience! Could you take 30 seconds to leave us a quick review?

[GOOGLE REVIEW LINK]

- The [Practice Name] Team
```

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create a friendly SMS review request (under 160 characters if possible) for 
clients who just had a [TREATMENT TYPE] appointment at my medspa.

Our brand voice is: [warm/professional/clinical/fun]
Practice name: [NAME]
We want to emphasize: [what makes your experience special]

Keep it:
- Short and mobile-friendly
- Grateful but not desperate
- Easy to say yes to

Include a placeholder for the Google review link.
```

---

### Template B: Value-Add

**Template:**
```
[First Name], thank you for choosing [Practice Name]! 🌟

Quick question - how did everything go today?

Your feedback helps us serve you better AND helps other people find us!

Leave a review: [LINK]

(Takes 30 seconds!)
```

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create an SMS review request that emphasizes how their review helps others 
find us. Treatment was [TREATMENT TYPE].

Our unique value proposition is: [what sets you apart]
Typical client pain point before finding us: [common problem]

Make them feel like they're helping the community by reviewing, not just 
doing us a favor. Keep it under 160 characters if possible.
```

---

### Template C: Incentive-Based (Use Sparingly)

**Template:**
```
Hi [First Name]! We hope you loved your visit today!

Leave us a Google review in the next 24 hours and we'll enter you to win 
[PRIZE] in our monthly drawing! 

Review here: [LINK]

Thanks for being awesome! ⭐
```

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create an SMS review request with a monthly giveaway incentive.

Our prize is: [MONTHLY DRAWING PRIZE like: free treatment, gift card, product bundle]
Value: [$X]

Make it exciting but compliant (mention it's a drawing, not guaranteed). 
Keep it short and action-oriented.

Note: Only use this template for hard-to-get-reviews clients, not everyone.
```

---

## PART 3: EMAIL TEMPLATES (Touch 2 - 24 Hours Later)

### Template A: Story-Focused

**Subject Line:** How did we do, [First Name]?

**Body:**
```
Hi [First Name],

Thank you for choosing [Practice Name] for your [treatment type] yesterday!

We're on a mission to help [NUMBER] more people in [YOUR CITY] discover 
[THE TRANSFORMATION/BENEFIT YOU PROVIDE], and your feedback helps us get there.

Would you take 2 minutes to share your experience on Google? Your review 
helps others who are researching [treatment] find us and feel confident 
about their decision.

[BUTTON: Leave a Review]

If you had any concerns about your experience, please reply to this email. 
We want to make sure everything was perfect!

Gratefully,
[Your Name]
[Practice Name]
```

**AI PROMPT TO CUSTOMIZE:**
```
Create an email review request for clients who had [TREATMENT] 24 hours ago.

Our mission/story: [Why you do what you do]
The transformation we provide: [End benefit/outcome]
Location: [City/Region]
Our tone: [Brand voice]

Make it:
- Personal and story-driven
- Focused on helping others, not just us
- Include a safety net for negative feedback (reply to email)
- Professional but warm

Length: 100-150 words max
```

---

**Subject Line:** Join [NUMBER]+ happy clients! ⭐

in [CITY], and we're building a community of people who are [FEELING/RESULT].

[BUTTON: Share Your Experience]

Thank you for being part of the [Practice Name] family!

[Your Name]

- Years in business: [X]
- Star rating: [X.X]

Make them feel like part of something bigger. Length: 100-150 words.
```

**Subject Line:** Love your results? Share them! ✨

**Body:**
```

How are you feeling after your [treatment] appointment?

If you're loving your results (or even if you're just starting to see them),

transformations!

Thank you!

[Practice Name]

Make it:
- Results and transformation focused
- Include option to submit before/after photos
- Enthusiastic about their progress

Length: 100-150 words
```

- Personal and from the individual provider
- Includes both a check-in and review request
- Feels genuine, not scripted
- Under 160 characters if possible

```

### Moment 1: At Checkout (Every Client)

**Script Template:**
```

leaving us a quick Google review? I can text you the link right now!"

- Easy to say "yes" to
